items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: playing Charlie Parker or Duke Ellington in the basement... Glenn Miller, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, they had played that music for a long time before they recorded it... Duke was the inspiration but Billy was the guy that really was the orchestrator.

ctx.x: In what parts of the country?

Well as soon as you get down below Washington I guess, down to Virginia, then it was all very difficult. But we were so much into the music, we weren’t thinking about that you know. That’s the wonderful thing about a lot of the guys that came before us, that © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

had more of those problems than we did. The music was so important to them that they just rode right through all of that. Music is like that. It’s really wonderful. It’s above everything. It’s above wars, it’s above racism, it’s above everything. Because see in the war, the guys that were having the jam sessions in the basement in Germany, the Germans, if they had been caught they would have been killed. They were still having jam sessions, playing Charlie Parker or Duke Ellington in the basement with the windows…

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Finally he asked me to join the band, but I wasn’t available at the time.

ctx.x: Duke. That was his professional name. He was a very talented guy. He played all the instruments. He taught me to play trombone. He played saxophone, trombone. He sang. He could play just about anything he put his hands on. I remember he’s the one that taught me to do the circular breathing and multiphonics, which is playing more than one note at a time. He taught me those things. The kids always ask me in school, how do you do that? How do you do those multiphonics and that circular breathing? I say it’s a lot…

was a saxophone player that played very beautiful saxophone and wrote some wonderful arrangements. Then the real genius of the family was the next brother over me, Maceo Hampton. Maceo was a real – a person that had total recall. He remembered everything that he saw when he went to the movies, everything that he heard. One time, he remembered everything. He also – he wrote a lot of wonderful music. He played all of the instruments in the family band. He played trumpet, trombone, saxophone – tenors, baritones,…
